title: Sifuna answers critics of his US tour as filings show diaspora fundraising plan; Dallas is next
key_points: Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna told Kenyans in Maryland he will not stay away from the US because there are 'no votes here'.
US filings show a plan to raise money from Kenyans in North America for his movement, Kenyan media report.
The tour moves to Dallas for a Thanksgiving dinner on November 27, then Houston, Seattle and California.
Visiting the US Embassy in Nairobi? It is closed for visa and consular services on November 26 (Thanksgiving).
content:
Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has told Kenyans in the United States that their views matter, even though few of them vote. He spoke in Maryland, one stop on a US tour that has now passed through New Jersey, Pennsylvania and the Washington, DC area. Sifuna plans to run for president in 2027.

What he said in Maryland

The Star and Mwakilishi both reported that Sifuna answered people who say politicians should not spend time in the diaspora because Kenyans abroad cast few votes.

"I don't want to be told not to come to the US on the reason that there are no votes here," he said, according to both outlets.

He also rejected advice that he should be "nicer" to win the presidency. He said the rules of his party, ODM, and of the Linda Mwananchi Movement he now leads, expect leaders to speak out against wrongdoing. The reports did not name the exact venue or date of the Maryland meeting.

What the US filings show

The Nation reported this week that US filings describe a plan to raise money from Kenyans abroad for Sifuna's campaign. Mwakilishi carried the same report.

According to Streamline Feed, which cites Tuko, the papers were filed with the US Department of Justice on October 28 under the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA). This US law asks people who do political work in America for a foreign politician or party to register and say what they do. Filing is a legal requirement, not a sign of wrongdoing.

Streamline Feed says the filing names Gilbert Shanga, a Kenyan based in Hackettstown, New Jersey, as coordinator. His listed tasks include arranging political meetings, encouraging fundraising among Kenyans in North America and meeting US officials. No amounts of money have been reported. These details come from one outlet and KASS-mtv could not check the filing itself. Sifuna's team has not commented publicly on the reports.

Background: according to Streamline Feed, Sifuna took over The Equitable Party in October, and delegates voted on November 13 to rename it the Linda Mwananchi Movement.

Where the tour goes next

Capital FM published this schedule for the rest of the tour:

  • November 27, Dallas: Thanksgiving dinner at the Mar Thoma Event Center.
  • November 29, Houston: women's meeting and a town hall.
  • December 3–4, Seattle area: Federal Way and Renton.
  • December 5, San Francisco Bay Area: town hall and gala in Oakland.
  • December 7, Silicon Valley: closing dinner.

Plans can change, so check with local organisers before you travel.

Why it matters

More politicians are visiting the US ahead of the 2027 election. For Kenyans in America, these meetings are a chance to ask questions about issues that affect them directly, such as consular services, the cost of sending money home and whether diaspora voting will be expanded.

Quick travel note

According to Mwakilishi, the US Embassy in Nairobi has suspended visa and consular services on Thursday, November 26, for the US Thanksgiving holiday. If you or your family have an appointment, check the embassy's website for the new date.
